metadata.note: El Paso and Southwestern Railroad (Arizona road, El Paso - Douglas extension, Arizona and New Mexico copper branches), its predecessor the Arizona and South Eastern (1889-1901), and the Southern Pacific from Nov 1 1924. Drawn exactly to the research report's drawable: fields, including its [OPEN] and [ANCHOR] markers. The EP&SW's New Mexico lines north of El Paso (El Paso - Tucumcari, Dawson, Capitan, Cloudcroft) are in el_paso_and_northeastern_railway.geojson (dataset PR #320) and are not repeated here. Research report: research/branches/el_paso_and_southwestern_railroad.txt.
metadata.operator_split: Rule 4 splits at Jul 1 1901 (A&SE -> El Paso and Southwestern; ICC says EP&SW operated from Jul 1 1901 and bought the A&SE Jun 17 1902, Wikipedia says the A&SE was renamed Jun 25 1901 - the split is drawn at 1901 either way, because that is when the trains' name changed) and at Nov 1 1924 (Southern Pacific control Oct 31 1924). The El Paso and Southwestern Company's 1908-1912 operating lease of its own railroad (same name and management) is NOT a split; nor is the 1910 Mexico & Colorado purchase (no M&C-operated passenger year). Colours, pulled by script: El Paso and Southwestern #B3592B read from the sibling layer el_paso_and_northeastern_railway.geojson on dataset branch claude/add-el-paso-and-northeastern-railway (PR #320, not yet merged); Southern Pacific #C1272D read from the existing "Southern Pacific Railroad" features in data/; Arizona and South Eastern #3E6FA8 is new and a script confirmed no other company in data/ or in that sibling file uses it. Segment years are inclusive, so an EP&SW segment ending 1924 and an SP segment starting 1924 both draw in 1924, as in the sibling layer. One-year [ANCHOR] spans are encoded start == end, the convention already used by 521 segments in data/ (e.g. minneapolis_and_st_louis_railway.geojson).
metadata.existing_layer_check: No feature in data/ draws this railroad (report's check, confirmed by grep for El Paso and Southwestern, Arizona and South Eastern, Bisbee, Tombstone, Hachita, Clifton). Not edited, but recorded: (1) crip-golden-state-route (chicago_rock_island_pacific.geojson) draws the Golden State 1902-1968 only via Deming and Lordsburg, whereas in the Feb 1952 Official Guide R.I.-S.P. No. 3 ran El Paso - Douglas - Bisbee Junction - Tucson over this layer's sp-mescal-douglas-el-paso, so its geometry is the wrong alignment for at least part of 1924-1961 (Wikipedia: the train "sometimes" used each route); its segment-1 note also implies SP ran El Paso - Tucson from 1902, which on the Douglas route would have been EP&SW-hauled. (2) southern_pacific_sunset_route.geojson: between about Rita Ranch (-110.83, 32.11) and Mescal its geometry runs within 150 m of the ex-EP&SW Tucson line for 23.5 mi - the two companies' lines ran side by side there and were paired as one double track by the SP from 1925, so the overlap is physical, not a defect in either layer.
omitted: Arizona and South Eastern Fairbank - Benson ([2a]): no A&SE passenger year confirmed - drawable NONE.
Southern Pacific on the Bisbee Branch ([4c]): no SP-era rail passenger year; Bisbee was served by bus from Bisbee Junction by 1951.
The Bisbee Junction (Osborn) - Don Luis link and the Corta - Warren - Lowell loop: part of the undated pre-1910 realignment; no passenger year for them specifically.
Southern Pacific Tucson - Mescal ([6c]): half of the SP paired main line, already drawn by southern_pacific_sunset_route (report recommendation).
Southern Pacific Douglas - Kelton ([10c]), Kelton - Courtland ([11c]), Deming Branch ([13c]), Tyrone Branch ([14c]): no SP-era passenger year confirmed.
Deming - Burro Mountain Junction (Santa Fe Silver City branch, EP&SW trains by trackage rights 1914-c.1924): foreign track; not drawn.
Naco Junction - Naco, Naco Junction - French, Fairbank spurs, Douglas smelter trackage, Apache Powder spur: freight/industrial, no passenger evidence (Rule 1).
Arizona and New Mexico years before EP&SW operation (Hachita - Lordsburg - Clifton from 1905): belong to the arizona_and_new_mexico_railway queue entry.
Arizona & Colorado (SP subsidiary, Cochise - Kelton - Gleeson): a separate road, not EP&SW.
Nacozari Railroad (Agua Prieta - Nacozari, Sonora) and the 1902 EP&SW special to Cananea: in Mexico, out of scope (Rule 9).
Golden State / Imperial through trains as separate features: covered by sp-mescal-douglas-el-paso.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Written to Rule 1 from the start: Benson - Douglas SP freight after 1961 (and San Pedro & Southwestern from 1992), Tombstone freight to 1961, Deming Branch 1924-1929, the Arizona Eastern on Lordsburg - Clifton today, and all industrial spurs are not drawn.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Not applicable - steam from opening (A&SE 4-4-0 No. 1).
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends - last CONFIRMED years, not known ends: epsw-fairbank-forrest-original 1902, epsw-bisbee-branch 1902, sp-mescal-douglas-el-paso 1961 (1963 per secondary lists), sp-benson-branch 1951, sp-hachita-lordsburg 1939, sp-lordsburg-clifton 1951.

[OPEN] starts - first CONFIRMED years: epsw-fairbank-forrest 1910 (realignment date between 1902 and 1910 unknown), epsw-douglas-el-paso 1904 (opened Dec 1902 / Mar 1903), epsw-benson-branch 1912 (bracket 1901-1912).

[ANCHOR] single years: epsw-fort-huachuca-branch 1917, sp-fort-huachuca-branch 1939, epsw-kelton-courtland 1911, epsw-deming-branch 1924, epsw-tyrone-branch 1924, epsw-hachita-lordsburg 1924, epsw-lordsburg-clifton 1924.
Bisbee rail passenger service 1903-1924 is near-certain but unproven: a Bisbee Daily Review (Chronicling America, 1901-1922) EP&SW timecard, or the 1910/1924 EP&SW public timetables, would settle it.
A&SE -> EP&SW operator date: Jul 1 1901 (ICC operation) vs Jun 25 1901 (Wikipedia renaming) vs Jun 17 1902 (ICC sale).
Tombstone Branch 1903-1924 is interpolated between the 1903 opening and the SP mixed; end 1960 (Wikipedia list) vs 1961 (hmdb marker).
Tyrone: ICC trackage-rights payments end Oct 1 1923, yet the 1924 public timetable lists Tyrone.
Year the EP&SW began operating the Arizona & New Mexico (acquired "1922").
Fowler AZ route 26 legend defines only a/b/w; reading c/d/t there as the SP general 1939G/1953t/1961t is the report's inference.
Geometry: which of the parallel Benson - Fairbank grades and which of the paired Tucson - Mescal tracks is ex-EP&SW was taken from OpenHistoricalMap, not checked against a valuation map.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, February 1952 (cached copy, read via research/guidecheck.py)

properties.line: Arizona and South Eastern: Fairbank – Bisbee
properties.speed_source: Estimated: ~25 km/h for a branch-line mixed train; not from a timetable's running times.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-11-25) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py (railtrace degree tiles + fetch_operator_ways for old_railway_operator EP&SW/El Paso/Southwestern/SP/A&SE spellings - only "Southern Pacific Railroad" and "SP" exist in the region - plus fetch_gap over every lifted stretch for railway=abandoned grades, rail-trails and OHM ways; OSM ways named "SP (EPSW)" / "El Paso & Southwestern" and OHM ways named "El Paso and Southwestern Railroad" were treated as the company's own).
properties.geometry_quality: Fairbank - Charleston - Lewis Springs - Naco Junction - Don Luis - Bisbee, the original 1889 line. Traced 36.8 mi against 36.20 mi documented (ICC). Two straight-line legs, approximated: Naco Junction grade end - Don Luis, 1.5 mi (the A&SE grade is mapped in OSM for only its first 2.5 mi from Naco Junction); and the last 1.3 mi from the end of mapped track north of Don Luis/Lowell into Bisbee (lost to the Lavender Pit and the town), drawn to the Bisbee town centre because the A&SE depot site was not located. The rest runs on OSM railway=abandoned grades (22.1 mi), the San Pedro Trail rail-trail (5.4 mi) and abandoned ways tagged for the later Union Pacific/San Pedro & Southwestern (5.6 mi) between Fairbank and Lewis Springs - the same grade the EP&SW and SP later used. Station points (geocodes checked: localities/hamlets, Fairbank hand-pinned because Nominatim returned its cemetery) lie within 0.3 km of the line except Bisbee (the straight leg ends on it).

segments.note: Arizona and South Eastern (Copper Queen Consolidated / Phelps Dodge) passenger service, from the official opening Feb 1 1889: one daily-except-Sunday mixed train carrying one or both of the line's coaches (Sept 1889 Official Guide: Bisbee 7:00am - Fairbank 9:30am; timetables of Mar 1890 and Nov 1892 also quoted). Steam from opening. Ends at the Jul 1 1901 change to El Paso and Southwestern operation - an operator change, not a service end (ICC: EP&SW operated from Jul 1 1901 and bought the A&SE Jun 17 1902; Wikipedia calls it a renaming Jun 25 1901 - conflict recorded in metadata). headway_min 1440 = one train a day each way, from the quoted timetables.
sources: Segment-level: this segment's note names the source for its dates (as established in the research report research/branches/el_paso_and_southwestern_railroad.txt; not re-read while tracing). Opening and 1889-1892 timetables from the A&SE history site quoting the Official Guide; operator dates from the ICC valuation.

properties.line: El Paso and Southwestern: Fairbank – Forrest (via Naco Junction)
properties.speed_source: Estimated: ~50 km/h for a single-track desert main line carrying through and local trains; not from a timetable's running times.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-11-25) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py (railtrace degree tiles + fetch_operator_ways for old_railway_operator EP&SW/El Paso/Southwestern/SP/A&SE spellings - only "Southern Pacific Railroad" and "SP" exist in the region - plus fetch_gap over every lifted stretch for railway=abandoned grades, rail-trails and OHM ways; OSM ways named "SP (EPSW)" / "El Paso & Southwestern" and OHM ways named "El Paso and Southwestern Railroad" were treated as the company's own).
properties.geometry_quality: The ORIGINAL main line on the A&SE route: Fairbank - Lewis Springs - Naco Junction - Don Luis - Galena - Forrest, later bypassed by the Hereford - Naco - Osborn line. Traced 45.6 mi against about 42.9 mi documented (Fowler route 31 Lewis Springs - Forrest 32.3 mi + Fairbank - Lewis Springs ~10.6 mi), about 6% long. One straight-line leg, approximated: Naco Junction grade end - Don Luis, 1.5 mi. The rest is on OSM railway=abandoned grades and the San Pedro Trail; the Don Luis - Forrest stretch follows an abandoned grade east of Don Luis that is taken to be the original line (it is the only mapped grade linking the two; not confirmed against a historical map).

segments.note: El Paso and Southwestern operation from Jul 1 1901 (continuous from the A&SE service) on the original alignment to Don Luis and on to Forrest and Douglas. Fowler: "Service to Forrest 1902G"; Banning, Packard, Naco Junction and Don Luis carry letter a = 1902 Official Guide. [OPEN] 1902 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Trains ran on this alignment until an undated realignment onto the Hereford - Naco - Osborn line (ICC line changes Forrest - Lewis Springs and Don Luis - Osborn), some time between 1902 and 1910. headway_min is an estimate (about two trains a day each way), not from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: this segment's note names the source for its dates (as established in the research report research/branches/el_paso_and_southwestern_railroad.txt; not re-read while tracing). Fowler route 31 station letters (1902 Official Guide); ICC valuation line changes.

properties.line: El Paso and Southwestern: Bisbee Branch
properties.speed_source: Estimated: ~30 km/h for a short single-track branch; not from a timetable's running times.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-11-25) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py (railtrace degree tiles + fetch_operator_ways for old_railway_operator EP&SW/El Paso/Southwestern/SP/A&SE spellings - only "Southern Pacific Railroad" and "SP" exist in the region - plus fetch_gap over every lifted stretch for railway=abandoned grades, rail-trails and OHM ways; OSM ways named "SP (EPSW)" / "El Paso & Southwestern" and OHM ways named "El Paso and Southwestern Railroad" were treated as the company's own).
properties.geometry_quality: Don Luis - Bisbee only, the approach the 1901-1902 trains used from the original line. Traced 3.5 mi; no documented figure for this piece alone (Fowler route 32, Bisbee Junction - Bisbee, is 7.9 mi, but the Bisbee Junction (Osborn) - Don Luis link belongs to the later realignment and is not drawn). Straight-line leg, approximated: the last 1.3 mi into Bisbee, from the end of mapped track (the alignment is lost to the Lavender Pit) to the Bisbee town centre; the depot site was not located. The Warren loop (Corta - Warren - Lowell) is not drawn - no passenger year for it.

segments.note: El Paso and Southwestern service into Bisbee, the reason the railroad existed, continuous from the A&SE. Proven only by Fowler's 1902 Official Guide letters on the route-31 stations; Fowler route 32 (Bisbee Branch) has only working-timetable letters (1910w, 1926w), which list stations and are not passenger evidence. [OPEN] 1902 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Service almost certainly continued through the EP&SW era (Bisbee depot photographed in the 1920s), but no dated public timetable naming Bisbee with a rail time was found; by 1951 the Official Guide routes Bisbee passengers by bus to Bisbee Junction. No Southern Pacific-era rail passenger year is confirmed, so nothing is drawn after 1902. headway_min is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: this segment's note names the source for its dates (as established in the research report research/branches/el_paso_and_southwestern_railroad.txt; not re-read while tracing). Fowler routes 31/32 letters; Feb 1952 Official Guide through-car tables (bus to Bisbee Jct).

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-11-25) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py (railtrace degree tiles + fetch_operator_ways for old_railway_operator EP&SW/El Paso/Southwestern/SP/A&SE spellings - only "Southern Pacific Railroad" and "SP" exist in the region - plus fetch_gap over every lifted stretch for railway=abandoned grades, rail-trails and OHM ways; OSM ways named "SP (EPSW)" / "El Paso & Southwestern" and OHM ways named "El Paso and Southwestern Railroad" were treated as the company's own).
properties.geometry_quality: Fairbank - Charleston - Lewis Springs - Hereford - Naco - Bisbee Junction (Osborn) - Crook - Forrest. Traced 49.8 mi; with Forrest - Douglas (9.7 mi) that is 59.5 mi against 58.8 mi documented Fairbank - Douglas (Fowler route 26, mp 1048.2 - 1107.0). No straight-line leg: 28.9 mi on OSM abandoned ways tagged for the Union Pacific (the last owner before the San Pedro & Southwestern), 13.9 mi on untagged abandoned grade, 5.4 mi on the San Pedro Trail rail-trail, the rest on short OHM/SP&SW pieces. The drawn track is the line as last abandoned (post-1992 San Pedro & Southwestern); no later realignment is known but none was searched for.

segments.note: El Paso and Southwestern main line on the Hereford - Naco - Osborn alignment. Fowler letter a (1910 EP&SW public timetable) on Charleston, Lewis Springs, San Pedro, Hereford, Stark, Naco, Osborn, Crook, Forrest, Calumet and Douglas; b (1924 EP&SW public timetable). [OPEN start] 1910 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - service probably began earlier but no source proves an earlier year. Do not extend without evidence. The realignment from the original A&SE route is undated (between 1902 and 1910), so 1903-1909 is left undrawn on both alignments. Ends when the Southern Pacific took control Oct 31 1924 and operated from Nov 1 1924. headway_min is an estimate (through trains plus a local), not from a timetable.

segments.note: The Douglas extension (built 1900-01): Fowler "Douglas Yard 1901G" (Douglas in the 1901 Official Guide); 1910 and 1924 EP&SW public timetable letters on Calumet and Douglas. The Douglas depot (NRHP) opened Aug 1913. Drawn from 1901 although Wikipedia gives 1900 for the extension - 1901 is the first proven year. Ends at Southern Pacific control (Nov 1 1924). headway_min is an estimate.

properties.line: El Paso and Southwestern: Douglas – El Paso
properties.speed_source: Estimated: ~50 km/h for a single-track desert main line carrying through and local trains; not from a timetable's running times.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-11-25) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py (railtrace degree tiles + fetch_operator_ways for old_railway_operator EP&SW/El Paso/Southwestern/SP/A&SE spellings - only "Southern Pacific Railroad" and "SP" exist in the region - plus fetch_gap over every lifted stretch for railway=abandoned grades, rail-trails and OHM ways; OSM ways named "SP (EPSW)" / "El Paso & Southwestern" and OHM ways named "El Paso and Southwestern Railroad" were treated as the company's own).
properties.geometry_quality: Douglas - Rodeo - Animas - Hachita - Hermanas - Columbus - Mastodon - Anapra - El Paso Union Depot. Traced 215.8 mi against ~216 mi documented (Fowler AZ 26 + NM 23 mileposts). No straight-line leg: 149.8 mi on ways named for the EP&SW (OSM "SP (EPSW)" abandoned grade and OHM "El Paso and Southwestern Railroad"), 59.8 mi on untagged abandoned grade (Douglas - Rodeo, Columbus area), 5.3 mi of untagged OHM rail, under 1 mi of modern track at Douglas. Line lifted 1961-63; the drawn grade is the line as abandoned. The last ~2 mi into El Paso Union Depot run on track the trace shares with the SP's own line (today's UP) - the EP&SW's separate Anapra - El Paso track is not distinguished there. LATER ALIGNMENT: El Paso Union Depot opened in 1906; 1904-1906 trains used an earlier El Paso station that is not drawn separately.

segments.note: El Paso and Southwestern El Paso extension. Construction completed Dec 1902; Texas portion "placed in service March 1, 1903" (american-rails); first PROVEN passenger year 1904 (Fowler "Vista [Corona 1904G]"; Animas 1905G), then 1910 and 1924 EP&SW public timetable letters along the line. [OPEN start] 1904 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - service probably began earlier but no source proves an earlier year. Do not extend without evidence. 1903 is likely but not proven by a timetable. The "El Paso & Southwestern Flyer" was the first train out of El Paso Union Depot (1906; uncited timeline). Ends at Southern Pacific control (Nov 1 1924). headway_min is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: this segment's note names the source for its dates (as established in the research report research/branches/el_paso_and_southwestern_railroad.txt; not re-read while tracing). Fowler NM route 23 / AZ route 26 letters; american-rails for the 1903 Texas opening; El Paso railroad timeline (uncited) for 1902/1906.

properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-11-25) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py (railtrace degree tiles + fetch_operator_ways for old_railway_operator EP&SW/El Paso/Southwestern/SP/A&SE spellings - only "Southern Pacific Railroad" and "SP" exist in the region - plus fetch_gap over every lifted stretch for railway=abandoned grades, rail-trails and OHM ways; OSM ways named "SP (EPSW)" / "El Paso & Southwestern" and OHM ways named "El Paso and Southwestern Railroad" were treated as the company's own).
properties.geometry_quality: EP&SW Tucson depot (Congress St) - Vail - Pantano - Mescal - Whetstone - Fairbank. Traced 64.4 mi against 64.6 mi (Fowler mp 983.6 - 1048.2) / 66 mi (ICC). No straight-line leg: 38.4 mi on OHM ways (the 1945-abandoned EP&SW entry into Tucson; Mescal - Fairbank, OHM-dated 1913-1970), 25.6 mi on untagged OSM track/grade. SHARED CORRIDOR: between about mile 12 (near Rita Ranch) and Mescal, 23.5 mi of this line lies within 150 m of the existing southern_pacific_sunset_route geometry - the SP's and EP&SW's lines ran side by side there (paired as one double track from 1925) and today's UP main uses parts of both; which modern track is ex-EP&SW was taken from OHM, not confirmed against a valuation map. LATER ALIGNMENT: Tucson - Mescal is drawn on track still in use, possibly with post-1924 line changes.

segments.note: El Paso and Southwestern Tucson line, built 1910-12 when Tucson replaced Benson as the western terminus. Last spike Oct 31 1912; first scheduled train arrived in Tucson Nov 20 1912 (Wikipedia, american-rails). Fowler 1924 EP&SW public timetable letters on Tucson (EPSW), Aldona, Pantano (EPSW), Cienega, Whetstone, Fairbank; the EP&SW Tucson depot (1913) "served travelers until 1924". Ends at Southern Pacific control (Nov 1 1924); the SP era is drawn only Mescal - Fairbank (sp-mescal-douglas-el-paso) because Tucson - Mescal became half of the SP's paired main line, already drawn by southern_pacific_sunset_route. headway_min is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: this segment's note names the source for its dates (as established in the research report research/branches/el_paso_and_southwestern_railroad.txt; not re-read while tracing). Opening from Wikipedia EP&SW and american-rails; Fowler routes 17, 18, 26 letters (1924 EP&SW public tt).

properties.geometry_quality: Fairbank - Tombstone. Traced 8.4 mi against 9.3 mi documented (ICC; Fowler mp 1048.2 - 1057.5); 6.7 mi on an OSM abandoned way named "El Paso & Southwestern", the rest untagged abandoned grade. No straight-line leg; the drawn end is about 1 km short of the documented terminal (grade not mapped into town).

segments.note: Track laid from Fairbank Mar 9 - Mar 24 1903; "passenger service began ... April 5, 1903" (Tombstone Times, a local-history journal, not a primary source). No EP&SW public-timetable letter falls on Tombstone between 1903 and 1924 (Fowler's only Tombstone letter is the 1924 WORKING timetable), so 1903-1924 is interpolated between the proven opening and the SP mixed train, not observed year by year. Ends at Southern Pacific control (Nov 1 1924). headway_min is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Benson - St. David - Curtiss - Fairbank, taken whole from one OpenHistoricalMap way (OHM 198198636, "Southern Pacific Railroad", start_date 1888, end_date 2002). Traced 19.6 mi against 19.10 mi documented (ICC, Fairbank - Benson). No straight-line leg. Two parallel grades run Benson - Fairbank (this one and the SP's 1882 New Mexico & Arizona); this one was chosen because OHM dates it 1888, the A&SE building year - not confirmed against a valuation map. LATER ALIGNMENT: Fowler notes a 1914 relocation of the branch; the drawn line is the post-1914 alignment as last abandoned, so for 1912-1914 it may not be the track then in use.

segments.note: El Paso and Southwestern Benson - Fairbank service; Benson was the EP&SW's western terminus and SP connection until the Tucson line opened in Nov 1912. Fowler route 27A letter a = 1912 EP&SW public timetable (St. Davids, Land), b = 1924 EP&SW public timetable. [OPEN start] 1912 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start - service probably began earlier but no source proves an earlier year. Do not extend without evidence. (start bracket 1901-1912). Ends at Southern Pacific control (Nov 1 1924). headway_min is an estimate.

segments.note: Army-post branch. Fowler "Buena 1917(EPSW)t" - Buena in the 1917 EP&SW public timetable. [ANCHOR] 1917 is the only year proven for this piece. Opening year not found; WWI troop movements are not public service and are not counted. headway_min is an estimate.

segments.note: Line opened Feb 1 1914 (american-rails); Burro Mountain RR leased to the EP&SW from Jan 1 1914, Santa Fe trackage rights from Jul 1 1914 (ICC). Conflict recorded: the ICC records Santa Fe trackage-rights payments only to Oct 1 1923, yet the 1924 public timetable lists Tyrone. No SP-era passenger year. headway_min is an estimate.

properties.line: Southern Pacific: El Paso – Mescal (via Douglas)
properties.speed_source: Estimated: ~50 km/h for a single-track desert main line carrying through and local trains; not from a timetable's running times.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-11-25) and OpenHistoricalMap, routed with opstrace.py (railtrace degree tiles + fetch_operator_ways for old_railway_operator EP&SW/El Paso/Southwestern/SP/A&SE spellings - only "Southern Pacific Railroad" and "SP" exist in the region - plus fetch_gap over every lifted stretch for railway=abandoned grades, rail-trails and OHM ways; OSM ways named "SP (EPSW)" / "El Paso & Southwestern" and OHM ways named "El Paso and Southwestern Railroad" were treated as the company's own).
properties.geometry_quality: Mescal - Fairbank - Hereford - Naco - Bisbee Junction - Douglas - Hachita - Columbus - El Paso: the same geometry as epsw-tucson-fairbank (from Mescal), epsw-fairbank-forrest, epsw-forrest-douglas and epsw-douglas-el-paso joined. Traced 301.4 mi against about 300 mi documented (Mescal - Fairbank 25.6 mi of Fowler's 64.6-mi Tucson line + 58.8 mi Fairbank - Douglas + ~216 mi Douglas - El Paso). Straight-line legs, approximated: only the three joins between traced pieces, 0.16 mi at Fairbank, 0.38 mi at Forrest and 0.32 mi through the Douglas yard. Each piece's own caveats apply (see those features): the last ~2 mi into El Paso Union Depot on track shared with the SP's own line; the Mescal end where the EP&SW line joined the SP paired main. Tucson - Mescal is not part of this feature (drawn by southern_pacific_sunset_route).

segments.note: Southern Pacific operation of the former EP&SW main line from Nov 1 1924 (control Oct 31 1924; bought outright and merged 1955). Through trains: the Golden State (R.I.-S.P. No. 3 in the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 9, El Paso - Douglas - Bisbee Junction - Tucson, with times at Columbus, Mastodon, Douglas, Bisbee Junction, Naco, Hereford, Lewis Springs, Fairbank, Whetstone) and the Imperial (Nos. 39/40, 1954: El Paso 2:15am - Douglas 6:10am - Bisbee Jct 6:50am - Tucson 8:40am, american-rails); the Douglas routing alternated with the SP's own line via Deming and Lordsburg. Fowler t (= 1961 public timetable, legend inferred) on Douglas, Bisbee Junction, Hereford, Rodeo, Animas, Hachita, Columbus; through trains "until December 1961" (Rogue Columnist); El Paso - Douglas abandoned 1961, rails removed 1963 (Wikipedia, Golden State). [OPEN] 1961 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Secondary station lists give "last Southern Pacific passenger service 1963" at Douglas (possibly a residual Tucson - Douglas train) - not drawn. Freight continued Benson - Douglas (SP, then the San Pedro & Southwestern from 1992); not drawn. headway_min is an estimate (two through trains each way plus locals).
